core_obligations: Compute the cohomology of the limit on B (proof lines 5645-5652): for U in B, H^m(F^bullet(U)) is the cohomology of the displayed complex of limits lim F_n^{m-2}(U) -> lim F_n^{m-1}(U) -> lim F_n^m(U) -> lim F_n^{m+1}(U) in the third spot.

Apply the inverse limit criterion (proof lines 5653-5659): assumptions (2)(a) and (2)(b) give the vanishing of R^1 lim needed for the More on Algebra lemma, which yields H^m(F^bullet(U)) = lim H^m(F_n^bullet(U)).
Stabilise the system (proof lines 5660-5663): by assumption (2)(c), H^m(F^bullet(U)) = H^m(F_n^bullet(U)) for all n >= n_0.

Pass to sheaves (proof lines 5664-5669): since B covers every object, the sheafifications of U -> H^m(F^bullet(U)) and of U -> H^m(F_n^bullet(U)) agree for n >= n_0, so the inverse system of sheaves H^m(F_n^bullet) is constant for n >= n_0 with value H^m(F^bullet), which proves the lemma.
proof_roadmap: Rewrite H^m of the limit complex at U in B as the cohomology of a complex of inverse limits.
Use the vanishing of R^1 lim in degrees m-2, m-1 and in degree m-1 of the cohomology to commute cohomology with the limit.
Use the stable range hypothesis to identify the limit with H^m of the n_0-th complex.
Sheafify and use that B covers everything to conclude constancy of the inverse system of sheaves.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the cohomology sheaf of a termwise inverse limit of complexes: under a covering family B of objects on which R^1 lim vanishes in the relevant degrees and the cohomology stabilises for n >= n_0, the maps H^m(F^bullet) -> lim H^m(F_n^bullet) -> H^m(F_{n_0}^bullet) are isomorphisms of sheaves (statement lines 5616-5642). The proof must combine three different hypotheses in the right order: the degree bookkeeping that produces the complex of limits at a single object (proof lines 5645-5652), the inverse-limit criterion applied to the two lower degrees and to H^{m-1} (proof lines 5653-5659), and finally sheafification together with the covering condition on B, which is what upgrades a pointwise computation on B to an isomorphism of sheaves (proof lines 5664-5669). The claim is H2: one carefully ordered application of a limit criterion plus a sheafification step.
